request.description: With ?replacementCategoryId=<same-type category>, the category's transactions AND debts are reassigned to the replacement before it's deleted. Without it, the request is rejected (400) if any transaction still uses the category; debts alone don't block it — they keep existing with categoryId = null.

request.description: If the transaction was generated for a debt installment (description "Parcela n/N - <debt name>"), that installment is paid (paymentDate = today) or unpaid to match and its debt's totals/status are recomputed, atomically. The response is still just the transaction — refetch GET /debts/:id to see the installment.

request.description: If the transaction is linked to a debt installment, the installment is kept and its transactionId becomes null; paying it later (POST /debts/:id/installments/:installmentId/pay) creates a fresh linked transaction.

request.description: Multipart field 'receipt', nothing else. JPEG/PNG/WebP (re-encoded to JPEG, max 2560 px, EXIF/GPS removed) or a complete PDF (stored as uploaded), detected from the file content, up to 10 MB. Replaces (and deletes) the previous receipt.

response.name: 200 OK — image re-encoded as JPEG, ≤ 10 MB (signature elided)
200 OK — PDF stored as uploaded (signature elided)
400 Bad Request — not a JPEG/PNG/WebP image or a PDF
400 Bad Request — no file in the 'receipt' field
413 Payload Too Large — file over 10 MB (Multer limit)

request.description: Public. The two plans with their price as configured in Stripe (amount is a decimal string in BRL) and the free-trial length, granted on the user's first subscription only. Cached for 1 h; while Stripe is down the last good list is served.

response.name: 503 Service Unavailable — payments aren't configured (development without Stripe keys)

request.description: The user's subscription, mirrored from Stripe by the webhook (never Stripe ids). Wrapped in { subscription } so "none" is { subscription: null }, not an empty body.

response.name: 401 Unauthorized — missing or invalid access token

request.description: Returns a Stripe-hosted Checkout page for the plan, to open in the app's in-app browser (card only; the app never shows a card form). 7-day free trial only if the user never had a subscription, locally or on Stripe. The subscription appears in /subscriptions/me once Stripe's webhook arrives.

response.name: 200 OK — open url in the in-app browser
400 Bad Request — validation failed
409 Conflict — already subscribed (also checked on Stripe, so a checkout whose webhook hasn't arrived yet counts; it's synced first)
502 Bad Gateway — Stripe failed (details only in the server log)

request.description: Schedules the cancellation for the end of the current period (never immediately); the user keeps the subscription until then and can reactivate it.

response.name: 200 OK — scheduled for the period end
404 Not Found — no trialing, active or pending subscription

request.description: Undoes a scheduled cancellation, whether it was set for the period end or for a date (Dashboard / Customer Portal).

response.name: 404 Not Found — nothing scheduled to cancel

request.description: Returns a Stripe Customer Portal page (update the card, see invoices) to open in the in-app browser — the way out of PAST_DUE.

response.name: 200 OK — open url in the in-app browser
404 Not Found — no Stripe customer yet (never started a checkout)

request.description: Not called by the app directly: Stripe's success/cancel/portal return URLs point here (Stripe only redirects to http(s) URLs), and this answers 302 to the app's deep link, which closes the in-app browser. result is allowlisted; anything else becomes canceled. Carries no data.

response.name: 302 Found — missing or unknown result becomes canceled

request.description: Called by Stripe, not by clients (hidden from Swagger). Reference example only: Stripe-Signature is an HMAC of the raw body with the endpoint's signing secret and a timestamp (5-minute tolerance), so this saved request can't be replayed as-is — it was signed with the test suite's fake secret. To exercise it locally: `stripe listen --forward-to {{baseUrl}}/webhooks/stripe` and `stripe trigger checkout.session.completed`. Handled: checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed — each re-reads the subscription from Stripe; others are acknowledged and ignored.
